_comment: Reviewed exceptions for scripts/verify_route_oracles.mjs. real = genuine street/data geometry (evidence in reason); known-bug = accepted pipeline artifact. Regenerate candidates with --write-whitelist, review in the triage gallery, prune stale entries as fixes land. Rebuilt 2026-07-27 against the BUG set after the shape matcher gained the strand-mean reference, and after that reference showed the WOBBLE residue is genuinely pipeline weave — correcting the blanket real verdicts of PR #36.

entries.reason: WOBBLE devM 9.3 m over a 360 m window. Re-reviewed 2026-07-27: the shape matcher now measures a reference across the CORRIDOR'S window instead of requiring it to grow a window of its own (refWeaveAcrossWindow). Window growth stops at the first segment more than 8° off the chord, which a raw trace (vertices every few metres) structurally cannot survive for 120 m — so the 2026-07-27 verdict recorded in PR #37 ("neither the strands nor their mean weave at all") measured the detector's density dependence, not the street. Measured over this window the data weaves two-sided by 6.7 m against a corridor devM of 9.3 m (ratio 0.72 ≥ 0.7): the corridor follows a weave the digitised traces already have.

WOBBLE devM 9.7 m over a 347 m window. Re-reviewed 2026-07-27: the shape matcher now measures a reference across the CORRIDOR'S window instead of requiring it to grow a window of its own (refWeaveAcrossWindow). Window growth stops at the first segment more than 8° off the chord, which a raw trace (vertices every few metres) structurally cannot survive for 120 m — so the 2026-07-27 verdict recorded in PR #37 ("neither the strands nor their mean weave at all") measured the detector's density dependence, not the street. Measured over this window the data's two-sided weave is only 3.5 m against a corridor devM of 9.7 m (ratio 0.36 < 0.7) — the data bows, the corridor waves, so this stays a pipeline artifact. Not reachable by re-centring reach (0.75–2.5 x cluster radius, hard and tapered weights) nor by simplification epsilon (0.1–4.4 m): the residual BUG count held at 11–17 across all 15 configurations measured on 2026-07-27, so the mechanism is not in either operator's tuning. Measured again on 2026-07-27 against the CORRIDOR'S window chord instead of the reference's own projection chord, the same traces weave two-sided by 9.7 m while the corridor weaves 3.2 m — three times as much, so this is very probably genuine street geometry. refWeaveAcrossWindow projects the window onto the reference, which slides its chord wherever the corridor is laterally offset (here the corridor sits 12.4 m from every strand, in the gap between carriageways that have diverged past the 24.4 m cluster radius while node re-centring still averages across 36.7 m), and so it under-reports. Which chord the class should measure against is open — tracked in product/PHASE.md.

The corridor tracks the digitised strands to within 1.8 m over this window — under the 4.4 m simplify budget — and all strands here are mutually coincident, so no node displacement is involved: the data bows 10.3 m one way and 4.1 m the other, and the pipeline's sub-budget displacement carries the weak side across the 3 m threshold. A boundary case of the class definition rather than a located defect.
